newsitem.title: UK: London freight rally looks like owners' false dawn.
newsitem.headline: London freight rally looks like owners' false dawn.

text.p: The Baltic Freight Index (BFI) opened September with a new drop, of nine points to 1091, supporting views that a firmer trend seen in August on dry cargo freight rates may have been a false dawn for owners.
"I can't see anything in today's fixtures to raise a glass to", one said. "It is dull and it is not helped by the Labour Day holiday in the United States".
Fixtures generally were sideways to easier with early Panamaxes in the Atlantic suffering and Capesize rates, which led the August rally on the BFI, failing to follow through on the upside.
Confirmation of this came from shipbrokers Simpson Spence and Young's weekly SSY Atlantic Capesize Index which was off 136 at 3,435 points in the latest week.
"There was limited new inquiry in the Atlantic market..." SSY commented. "Consequently spot rates weakened".
"There has been quite a lot of interest and activity in the Atlantic to Pacific routes, however not all the cargoes materialized and rates also dipped slightly".
Among Capers on Monday, grain trades fixtures included Crusader Venture 52,000/5 heavy grains U.S. Gulf/South Korea for mid-September to Tradigrain reported at $19.25.
This would be about in line with last week.

Brokers said they understood that Continental were open for U.S. Gulf/Japan and likely to fix soon after the Labour Day break, apparently for mid-to-late September, which would be an indicator to that key BFI index route.
"Grain houses are having the time of their lives", said one market participant.
But he added that, from an owners' perspective, a spate of reports on bigger harvests around the globe may offer a glimmer of hope.
Although the International Grains Council (IGC) was predicting lower Chinese imports, fuller silos in regions like the European Union suggested more short-term export activity.
Easier prices might also tempt out Third World buyers.
Timecharters remain weak compared with what could have been expected a few months ago, but little changed on recent levels with some slightly better than last done for equivalent fixings.
Among fixtures reported on Monday were 1982-built Hellas 139,609 dwt delivery Sines 5/15 October trip via Brazil redelivery Singapore-Japan Range for $11,900 daily.
Also a touch firmer was 1990-built Merchant Pride 69,458 to NSAC delivery U.S. Gulf 10-15 September trip redelivery Far East $11,750 daily plus $185,000.
Activity was thin on Biffex futures. Most traded October was down 21 at 1215 by 1445 GMT in volume of just 65 lots.
Brokers said Labour Day was subduing the market and the new drop on the BFI was in line with expectations about the physical market. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7729
